title: Private VPC: Egress Lattice and Operatorless Cutover Requirements
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Purpose: Define requirements and acceptance criteria for an operatorless upgrade/cutover flow for Private (VPC) deployments that can run under constrained egress policies (including zero-egress/air-gapped sites). This doc introduces the 'egress lattice' concept: a staged, per-subnet minimal-exposure policy that allows atomic handoffs during upgrades without requiring a full open-egress window. Scope: networking requirements (egress gates, DNS split-horizon, MTU), artifact distribution and provenance (signed manifests, checksums), upgrade sequencing (mirror staging, canary cutovers, graceful traffic migration), and operatorless recovery options (physical-media or pull-proxy fallback). Out-of-scope: full operator UI changes, paid support packaging, cloud-provider-specific IAM plumbing. Assumptions: customer runs Kubernetes-based Private Operator; cluster nodes may have no outbound internet by default; customers can provide an allowlist of egress endpoints or an internal mirror registry; KMS/HSM integration available for signing verification when required.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Operatorless bootstrap/upgrade completes without any transient open-egress window when customer provides a validated internal mirror registry and signed artifact manifests.

A2: When zero-egress is requested, the platform can accept artifacts via physical-media-import or via a customer-hosted pull-proxy; both paths must validate artifact signatures and checksums before applying upgrades.

A3: The egress lattice policy must allow per-subnet staged egress to exactly three endpoints (mirror registry, artifact-signing-OCSP endpoint, and registry-checksum endpoint) during a narrow timebox; this policy is configurable and documented.

A4: DNS split-horizon is supported: the control-plane URL and mirror registry hostnames resolve to private endpoints when deployed inside the VPC, and tests must validate correct resolution under both old and new DNS configurations.

A5: MTU/fragmentation constraints are documented and validated during pre-flight checks; firmware-level MTU mismatches must surface a blocking validation (prevent upgrade) unless operator approves manual override.

A6: Staged canary cutover: upgrades must support a 3-step rollout (control-plane canary, node pool canary, full pool cutover) with observable health checks and automatic rollback triggers on predefined SLO breaches (latency, error-rate, pod restart rate).

A7: Artifact provenance: all images and operator bundles used in the upgrade must be signed; the operator verifies signatures using either customer KMS keys or Redwood-verifiable chain. Unverified artifacts fail the upgrade and generate an actionable error with remediation steps.

A8: Telemetry: when running in air-gapped/limited-egress mode, a local telemetry snapshot is produced and available for customer download; a masked summary metric (no PII) may be optionally permitted to be uploaded if customer consents.

A9: Rollback: operatorless rollback path is supported and can be executed solely using local artifacts and previously captured cluster state snapshots; rollback completes within SLO defined in release notes.

A10: Documentation and runbook: release must include a concise runbook (pre-check, canary steps, rollback steps, verification commands) and a checklist for network teams to validate egress lattice policies prior to upgrade.
notes: 2025-02-12: Kickoff with Platform Eng and Security. Agreed to prototype egress lattice as policy layer integrating with CNI and operators' pre-flight checks.

2025-02-18: Design review feedback (Security): require signed manifests and optional KMS integration. Added physical-media fallback to scope after trade-off discussion: trade-off between complexity vs customer needs for fully air-gapped sites.
2025-02-24: Engineering spike (ENG-5581) validated mirror-based no-egress path for small private clusters. Observed additional DNS edgecases when control-plane endpoints are replaced during rollout.
2025-02-27: PM and Eng agreed to introduce a short-lived egress permit token model for non-zero-evidence customers; UX and operator UX to be handled in a follow-up ticket.
2025-03-03: Security review requested — initial security notes attached. Requesting sign-off on allowing OCSP/CRL queries to be optionally proxied to customer internal endpoints.
Follow-ups: create ENG tickets for CNI integration tests, add QA matrix for physical-media import, draft customer runbook, schedule customer beta for Q2.
Known trade-offs: implementing operatorless rollback increases complexity of replica-state snapshotting; initial rollout will limit support to K8s clusters >= v1.25 to reduce matrix surface.
Open questions: acceptable retention window for local telemetry snapshots; whether Redwood will escrow a key for customers that cannot provide KMS during beta.
